title: Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow
subtitle: Soma's inheritance returns

body: Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow is Konami's action role-playing adventure for Nintendo DS and a sequel to Aria of Sorrow. Soma Cruz is drawn back into danger by a cult seeking the return of a Dark Lord. Exploration unfolds across an interconnected castle, with equipment, experience and new abilities gradually expanding what Soma can reach. The side-on action retains the directness of a platform game, while its larger structure rewards returning to a familiar corridor with a power that changes the route through it.

The Tactical Soul system lets Soma acquire abilities from defeated creatures. An enemy is consequently more than an obstacle or a source of experience: it may provide a new attack or another useful effect. Equipment and soul choices allow the player to prepare for a particular fight, while the castle's passages encourage experimentation outside combat. A collection grows through ordinary exploration. The system gives repeated encounters an additional purpose, because the creature already recognised on screen can still have something valuable left to offer.

Dawn of Sorrow adds Magic Seals, patterns that must be traced with the stylus to finish important enemies. A boss encounter can therefore move from buttons to a brief drawing action at its conclusion. The second screen also makes information available while Soma continues exploring below. Konami combines these DS-specific gestures with the progression inherited from Aria of Sorrow. The central pleasure remains learning the castle and reshaping Soma's abilities, with the new hardware changing particular moments rather than the whole rhythm of the adventure.
